critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: The localization rule did not settle which visible edges belong to the upper-right green-covering container's top square. For this cycle, that face should yield a grasp axis near world (x,y)=(-0.047,0.1656) and square-edge yaw 0.2892, rather than my estimate (-0.058,0.160) and yaw 0.45. The target selection, open gripper, and approach height 0.20 were already settled; the missing connection was the precise top-face fit to the calibrated image, not additional historical memory.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
The failures occurred during open-hand approaches to correctly selected containers: initially to the red-covering container, and after replacing the first lifted container and retreating to clearance, to the green-covering container. The retained demonstration pair established the correct identities, and completed_lifts correctly distinguished the first target from the second. Nevertheless, the chosen approach centers were displaced by more than 1 cm, and the second approach also used an inaccurate square-edge yaw. This is a waypoint SUFFICIENCY failure in image localization, not a memory PREDICTABILITY failure or evidence that another historical field is needed.

Strengthen the existing top-face reconstruction rule for all open-hand approaches, including approaches after replacement. Instead of accepting an approximate four-corner selection or a fit to one ambiguous edge, fit a complete horizontal square jointly to the visible top-face boundary evidence. Generate candidate corners from the outer boundary of the upper horizontal face, excluding the lower rim, vertical walls, and inset or shaded markings. Intersect candidate corner rays with world z=0.05 m using the supplied calibration, and check that the resulting world edges form a square: opposite edges parallel, adjacent edges perpendicular, and edge lengths equal. Infer occluded corners from these constraints rather than substituting corners from another height or averaging the full silhouette. Recover the center and yaw from this constrained square.

Project the fitted square back into both current calibrated images. Prefer the fit whose projected upper-face edges agree with the visible boundaries in both views; do not average incompatible front and wrist estimates. An occluded or off-screen target in one view supplies no boundary constraint in that view. Where the current front view is obstructed, the retained settled demonstration image can corroborate the geometry of a target that has not been moved, using the fixed front-camera calibration. Use the square's world-space edge directions, not raw image slopes, for yaw, selecting the square-equivalent downward-hand yaw closest to zero. Apply this fit before committing the approach waypoint, not only before the later grasp descent. Preserve the existing approach height, gripper commands, target-order rules, lift counting, replacement, and clearance rules. Do not introduce stored target coordinates or episode-specific coordinate corrections.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Average the four reconstructed corners to obtain the grasp-axis x,y, and recover yaw from the reconstructed square edges. If corners are obscured, fit the square to visible top-face edges and check against the other calibrated view rather than averaging the silhouette. Use the current wrist-camera extrinsics for the wrist view. Command the open-hand approach at this reconstructed x,y and z=0.20 m.

fields.name: demonstration_reference
fields.description: At the video cycle, store an ordered pair of frame labels: the last frame showing the uncovered colored cubes, followed by the first frame showing the settled containers covering them. Retain this pair throughout execution. These images preserve the color-to-container correspondence, including targets obscured by the hand later. e.g. ["V16", "V32"]
fields.annotation: At the video cycle, store an ordered pair of frame labels: the last frame showing the uncovered colored cubes, followed by the first frame showing the settled containers covering them. Retain this pair throughout execution. These images preserve the color-to-container correspondence, including targets obscured by the hand later. e.g. ["V16", "V32"]

fields.name: completed_lifts
fields.description: Write zero at the video cycle. At an act cycle, increment the incoming count once only if this cycle's motion images show the closed hand lifting the next requested container from near z=0.063 m to near z=0.20 m, with the container moving with the hand and its cube exposed. A stationary elevated grasp or a downward motion is not another lift. Otherwise copy the incoming count, including after release and retreat. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment once at the act cycle showing a requested container successfully raised from grasp height to approximately z=0.20 m while held closed, exposing its cube. Count requested containers in instruction order. Do not increment on approach, grasp closure, lowering, release, or retreat. Retain the count otherwise. e.g. 1

texts.action:
At the video cycle write memory only. Execution begins with an open hand high above the table. Read the requested colors in instruction order and use demonstration_reference to associate each with its covering container. Match the uncovered cube locations to the covering events and settled arrangement, not to arbitrary container ordering; ignore extra containers. Use the current images to localize the corresponding container. Front-image right is positive world y.

Localize a resting container by reconstructing its upper horizontal square face on the world z=0.05 m plane. Identify that face's four outer corners, excluding vertical side faces and the lower rim; do not use the whole silhouette or the grasp TCP height as the reconstruction plane. For each corner pixel p=(u,v,1), compute the camera center C=-R^T t and world ray d=R^T K^{-1}p using the view's calibration. Intersect the ray with the face plane: X=C+((0.05-C_z)/d_z)d. Fit a complete horizontal square jointly to the visible upper-face boundary evidence, rather than accepting approximate independent corners or one ambiguous edge. Exclude inset or shaded markings as well as vertical walls and the lower rim. Use the ray-plane intersections to constrain a world-space square with parallel opposite edges, perpendicular adjacent edges, and equal edge lengths. Infer occluded corners from these square constraints, never from boundaries at another height. Obtain grasp-axis x,y from the fitted square's center and yaw from its world-space edge directions, not raw image slopes. Project the fitted square back into both current calibrated images and choose the fit whose upper-face edges agree with the visible boundaries; do not average incompatible front and wrist estimates. Use the current wrist-camera extrinsics for the wrist view. An occluded or off-screen target supplies no boundary constraint in that view. If the current front view is obstructed, the retained settled demonstration frame may corroborate a target's geometry using the fixed front-camera calibration, but only if that target has not moved since the demonstration. Apply this constrained fit before every open-hand approach, including the initial approach and approaches after replacement and clearance, as well as before grasp descent. Command the open-hand approach at the fitted center x,y and z=0.20 m. Use a downward hand, roll=3.1416 and pitch=0, with yaw aligned to the container's square sides, choosing the equivalent yaw closest to zero. Container grasp TCP height is approximately 0.0633 m. Approach and lift height is 0.20 m. Re-estimate the actual container center rather than using the achieved TCP x,y blindly: approach motions can undershoot by more than a centimetre.

Apply these state-dependent rules, using completed_lifts updated from the motion just observed:

If the hand is closed around a container at low grasp height, lift that container to z=0.20 with the gripper closed. Center the lift over the container's current x,y, preserving its aligned yaw. This rule takes precedence over selecting another target.

If a completed requested lift leaves a container held at z approximately 0.20 and further requested colors remain, lower it vertically at the current TCP x,y to z=0.070 and open the gripper at arrival; preserve the current orientation. Do not carry it to the next target or drop it from approach height.

If the gripper is open near z=0.070 following that replacement, retreat vertically at the current x,y to z=0.146 with the gripper open and orientation preserved. The next target is not approached laterally until this clearance is reached.

Otherwise, with an empty open hand, select requested color number completed_lifts+1. If not already above that container at approximately z=0.20, move to its center x,y at z=0.20 with aligned downward orientation and the gripper open. This includes the initial high pose and the post-release clearance pose. If already above the selected container at approach height, descend to its center x,y at z=0.0633 and close at arrival. At approach height, reconstruct the same top face again using the current calibrated wrist image, checked against the front view, to correct lateral undershoot. Descend directly to the reconstructed x,y at the grasp TCP height and close, without inserting an extra approach waypoint. The z=0.05 m reconstruction plane is distinct from the z=0.0633 m grasp TCP height.

After the final requested lift, keep holding the container; do not replace it. If another cycle arrives despite completion, wait briefly with the grasp unchanged.

For an ambiguous view, use the retained demonstration images and current wrist image together; do not guess a different container from proximity alone. If localization remains uncertain, make a safe open-hand upward clearance move before reassessing, or briefly wait if holding an object. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; any necessary gripper-only change must include at least 0.002 m of safe motion. If an action executed no steps, do not infer progress or increment the lift count.
